notes: Declarative only. This repo ships no benchmark runner, so nothing here is executed by CI — the verifier commands are plain shell, runnable by hand from a workspace that has the plugin provisioned.

Runner, sandbox and workspace settings are deliberately absent: naming a specific agent CLI and its flags here would describe a harness this repo does not have. Whatever harness runs this supplies its own.
Scope is install-and-look. It answers 'did the plugin land and can its entry points be found', and nothing at all about whether a pipeline run behaves.
Provisioning is expected to come from a marketplace inside the workspace, so a run never installs at global scope and never disturbs the operator's own plugin set.
The last verifier is a negative one: a commands/ directory would mean the skills-over-slash-commands move regressed, so its absence is asserted rather than assumed.

scenarios.title: The plugin lands and its entry points are reachable
scenarios.purpose: Show that agentic-sdlc provisions into a throwaway workspace and that its skills can be found, while starting no pipeline work at all.
scenarios.userInput: This workspace just had the agentic-sdlc plugin provisioned into it from a local marketplace. Have a look at what arrived. Tell me whether the plugin is reachable, whether the repo-guides skill is there, and whether the four run controls -- sdlc-guided, sdlc-auto, sdlc-runs, sdlc-preflight -- are present. I also want to know they are skills, not slash commands. Do not start an SDLC run of any kind; I am only asking you to look.
successChecklist: Says the plugin is installed, and can say how it got there.
Finds the repo-guides skill inside the plugin.
Establishes that the run controls are skills, with no slash commands involved.
Looks, reports, and stops — no pipeline is started, not even a first phase.
